newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National to hear from Treasury, RBNZ on economy.
newsitem.headline: National to hear from Treasury, RBNZ on economy.

text.p: Conservative National Party MPs will be briefed by senior Treasury and Reserve Bank officials on Tuesday on the second day of the party's annual three-day caucus retreat.
Treasury secretary Murray Horn and Reserve Bank deputy governor Murray Sherwin will address the caucus, a government spokesman said.
The caucus, being held at a motor inn 30 minutes drive west of Auckland, is then expected to discuss exporting, the economy and fiscal policy at a debate chaired by Finance Minister Bill Birch.
As part of its agreement with minor coalition partner New Zealand First, National has agreed to extra spending of NZ$1.2 billion in the 1997-98 year but has postponed $1 billion in planned tax cuts.
Business leaders and exporters have called for the government to reconsider its spending plans as a first step in restraining a rising New Zealand dollar.
The inflation band targeted by the Reserve Bank was widened to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent as part of the coalition deal.
The caucus is also scheduled to hear from Manufacturers' Federation chief executive Simon Arnold and Federated Farmers president Malcolm Bailey as part of its deliberations on the export sector.
The spokesman said the first caucus session on Monday spent time on education and communications issues.

The government is embroiled in controversy over Maori television station Aotearoa Television, with $4 million in new funding on hold pending investigations by the Serious Fraud Office and Commerce Ministry officials.
The New Zealand Herald reported on Tuesday that Prime Minister Jim Bolger said there was no proof of anything amiss at the station.
"No media or opposition parties have identified anything wrong at Aotearoa Television.
"There has been lots of speculation and innuendo but nothing else," Bolger told the Herald.
Communications Minister Maurice Williamson told journalists on his way into Monday's caucus meeting that investigations into the allegations were continuing.

"I'm not actually quite sure what some of the allegations are just yet but we are looking at them, and at the conclusion of those investigations there will be a report made to cabinet and cabinet will decide whether they confirm to continue funding the station," he said.
He said the funds were needed by February 6 if the station was to continue on air.
